digest._comment: 60, lowered from 65 the day remote-only filtering landed. Remote-only removed 36 of 82 open roles, so the pool shrank and the top score with it — 65 was hiding two genuinely remote roles sitting at 62. Same reasoning as the earlier 70→65 move. Raise it if the digest starts feeling padded; that is the signal, not the count.

titleGate._comment: A job must look like an engineering role from its TITLE alone. Without this, company boilerplate in the description (Vercel's footer mentions payments and ledgers on every posting) floats accountants and transport planners to the top of a keyword ranking.
titleGate._comment_customerFacing: Technical customer-facing titles are admitted deliberately. The gate exists to stop company boilerplate floating a Senior Accountant to the top of a keyword ranking, and it does — but it also silently rejected genuine technical customer-success and solutions roles before the scorer ever saw them, which for some applicants is their strongest category. A non-technical CSM role now reaches the scorer and is rejected there on fit instead, which costs a little quota and no accuracy.

dealbreakers._comment: Matched case-insensitively against title + description. A hit rejects the job BEFORE any scoring, so keep this list tight — every entry here is a job you will never see.
phrases: must reside in the united states
must be located in the us
authorized to work in the united states without sponsorship

locationRules._comment: eligible/ineligible are matched against the job's location string. Ineligible wins over eligible. Anything matching neither is 'unclear' and passes through to scoring, where the model judges it.
locationRules._countryLockNote: A location like 'Remote - India' or 'Remote: United States, Remote: Canada' is remote but country-locked. If a location says remote AND names a country he cannot work from, it is ineligible unless it also carries a global/EMEA/Africa token.
locationRules._remoteComment: remoteOnly: a city-only location is kept only if the posting itself mentions remote work. Set false to let the model judge city roles instead.

prescore._comment: Cheap deterministic pass. Only the top `llmBudget` survivors get an LLM call, so these weights control what the expensive stage ever sees.

_freshnessNote: Was 21, which dropped 4,419 of 6,257 postings. Age is a poor proxy for 'still open' — startup roles stay live for months — and src/verify.js now checks the link directly. Recency still earns a prescore bonus; it just no longer eliminates.
